owner_target_text: Aufbau von Simulationen (Marktdynamiken, Verhandlungsszenarien, strategische Konfliktsimulationen) mit mehreren spezialisierten Agenten, die autonom auf gemeinsamer Datenbasis agieren. Skalierbarer Parallelbetrieb auf einem Host ohne extremen RAM-Overhead durch geteilte Modellgewichte im Shared Memory.
what_was_actually_done: First experiment today with genuinely SPECIALIZED agents (distinct roles/capabilities with opposing objectives -- 2 'buyer_role' agents wanting a LOW price, 2 'seller_role' agents wanting a HIGH price) rather than interchangeable workers. Modeled a minimal 3-round price negotiation for a stated item, with each side reading the counterpart's most recent committed offer via the fabric (same GWT-style uptake pattern used in the earlier world-model simulation) before stating its next position.
two_real_bugs_found_and_fixed_during_the: First attempt: rounds 1-2 produced empty answers because the per-round wait (4.0s, copied from the earlier pipeline experiment's timing) was too short for THIS prompt's real decode+commit cycle (needs to express a dollar figure past the checkpoint's thinking-template overhead) -- fixed by extending to 9.0s.

Price extraction used a naive \d+ regex that misparsed comma-formatted numbers: '$1,200' was read as just '1' (stopping at the comma), giving a nonsensical extracted price of 1.0 -- fixed by stripping commas before matching.

genuine_finding_1_round_timing_reliabili.observation: Even after both fixes, only 1 of 3 rounds (round 2) actually produced real committed data in the final run; rounds 1 and 3 both showed empty answers despite identical code/timing for every round.
genuine_finding_1_round_timing_reliabili.honest_interpretation: This is a real, not-yet-fully-root-caused reliability characteristic of ROUND-BASED multi-agent interaction on this fabric: task injection happens in bursts spaced by the driver's own sleep, and with LEASE_TTL_SECONDS=8.0s while per-round waits here were 9.0s, coordinator leases for the negotiation scopes were plausibly expiring and needing self-renewal between rounds (the earlier use-case-2 fix should handle this, but recovery isn't necessarily instant within a single poll cycle). Not chased further given time constraints -- reported honestly as an open reliability question for round-based simulations specifically, distinct from the crash-resilience questions already resolved in use cases 1-2. A production version of this pattern would likely want the DRIVER to poll-and-wait for confirmed commitment before advancing to the next round, rather than a fixed sleep -- the same lesson already learned and applied in use case 2's edge-resilience experiment, not yet carried over to this one.

genuine_finding_2_specialization_did_not.observation: In the one round that DID land cleanly (round 2), the buyer offered exactly $1,200 and the seller asked exactly $1,200 -- the identical number, not two different, opposing positions.
genuine_finding_2_specialization_did_not.honest_interpretation: The mechanical specialization (distinct roles, distinct capabilities, distinct prompts explicitly stating opposite objectives) worked correctly at the infrastructure level. But the underlying small model did not actually produce differentiated strategic behavior between the two roles in the data collected -- consistent with use case 3's finding (differently-framed approaches converging on the same answer rather than genuinely diverging). This is a real, useful, and slightly cautionary finding for anyone planning multi-agent strategic simulations on a model this size: role-framing in the prompt does not reliably guarantee behaviorally distinct agents, and apparent 'agreement' between simulated adversarial roles should not be read as a meaningful negotiation outcome without independently verifying the roles are actually producing different reasoning, not just the same answer twice.

ram_scaling_measurement_-_honest_limitat.attempted: Compare Shared_Clean/RSS at a small fleet (4 nodes) against the 10-node fleets measured in use cases 1-2, to directly test the 'skalierbarer Parallelbetrieb ohne extremen RAM-Overhead' claim as node count grows.
ram_scaling_measurement_-_honest_limitat.why_the_direct_comparison_is_not_valid_a: The measurement was taken 2.0s after process launch, matching the exact same timing used in every other experiment today -- but unlike those experiments (which seeded tasks BEFORE spawning nodes, so real inference was already underway by the 2.0s mark), this negotiation experiment only seeds tasks INSIDE the round loop, AFTER the RSS check. At 2.0s, none of the 4 negotiation processes had performed any real inference yet, so their COW-shared weight pages were not yet faulted into resident memory (lazy paging) -- their measured RSS (~549MB) and Shared_Clean (~8MB) reflect an essentially idle, pre-work state, not a genuine 4-node-under-load data point. Comparing this directly against the 10-node runs' ~2.06GB RSS / ~1.48GB Shared_Clean (measured mid-load) would be misleading.
ram_scaling_measurement_-_honest_limitat.what_is_still_solidly_established: The 10-node, under-load figures from use cases 1-2 remain valid and real: ~1.48GB Shared_Clean per process (COW-shared, one physical copy), ~545MB real marginal RSS cost per additional loaded node. A proper apples-to-apples small-vs-large fleet comparison (both measured mid-load, after real inference has actually touched the weight pages) was not completed here due to time -- flagged as a genuine open item rather than silently presenting a flawed number as if it were a real finding.

net_conclusion_for_this_use_case.mechanically_proven: The fabric can host genuinely specialized, differently-capabilitied concurrent agents with opposing stated objectives and let them exchange positions over multiple real rounds via the same coordinator-commit/GWT-uptake mechanism proven earlier today.
net_conclusion_for_this_use_case.not_yet_reliable: Round-based multi-agent interaction spanning tens of seconds needs driver-side confirm-before-advance logic (not a fixed sleep) to avoid the kind of intermittent round-drop seen here -- a concrete, actionable next step, not just a vague caveat.
net_conclusion_for_this_use_case.not_yet_proven: That role-specialization at this model size produces genuinely differentiated strategic behavior rather than convergent, non-adversarial outputs -- the one clean data point collected argues against it, consistent with use case 3's finding, but this is a single data point and should be treated as a hypothesis worth further testing, not a settled conclusion.
net_conclusion_for_this_use_case.ram_scaling_claim: Still credibly supported by the solid 10-node figures from earlier use cases, but a direct small-vs-large comparison under matched conditions remains an open item.
